text:
dmitri: Quick question — we have a short-term contractor who needs to run a batch of evaluation jobs in project `ai-evals` for 7 days. They need to submit BigQuery jobs and impersonate a service account that owns the datasets, but we MUST prevent them from viewing any raw request payloads or unredacted logs. What's the least-privileged way to set this up?

maria: Prefer SA impersonation (iam.serviceAccounts.actAs) over sharing keys. Grant only the roles the job needs (BigQuery job submit + read dataset if required). Do NOT give logs viewer if you want to block raw payloads. Consider a custom role.

dmitri: Thx — specifically which bindings? Is it enough to give `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` on the service account and `roles/bigquery.jobUser` on the project?

leo: That combo is usually fine: grant `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` on the SA (so they can impersonate) + `roles/bigquery.jobUser` scoped to the dataset/project they operate on. If they need to read tables for eval inputs, add `roles/bigquery.dataViewer` only on the specific dataset.

sam: To your logging concern: removing `roles/logging.viewer` prevents access to Logs UI, but note that some logs are accessible via other APIs if users have cloud asset viewer or broader roles. Best practice: scope BigQuery permissions narrowly and avoid granting any org/project roles that include logging.

maria: If you must let them see aggregated metrics but not payloads, create a limited custom role for Logs that only allows `logging.logMetrics.list` and nothing that returns payload fields. But GCP logging APIs don't have fine-grained field-level controls — for true redaction you should route logs through a sink that redacts sensitive fields before storing in the destination the contractor can access.

dmitri: Got it. So plan: 1) create contractor SA `sa-evals-contractor@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com`; 2) grant contractor user account `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` on that SA; 3) grant `roles/bigquery.jobUser` on `projects/ai-evals`; 4) grant `roles/bigquery.dataViewer` only on `datasets/evals_inputs` if needed; 5) avoid any `logging.viewer`/org-level roles. Sound right?

leo: Yep. Also set an expiration (7 days) via IAM condition or automation to remove binding after 7 days. Example CLI for binding with no expiration (then automate removal):
```
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding ai-evals \
  --member='user:contractor@example.com' \
  --role='roles/iam.serviceAccountUser' \
  --condition=None
```
(we usually add a ticket id in the condition for auditability).

sam: We'll also create a log sink that redacts requestPayload fields and write to a separate project the contractor can see if they need aggregated logs. Ping me and I can set that up.

secbot: NOTICE: Remember to record the approval in the access request tracker (#access-requests) and attach the ticket ID. Ephemeral access should be recorded for audits. :white_check_mark:

dmitri: Thanks everyone — I'll put together a brief PR with the IAM bindings and an expiry job. Will @sam when ready to create the redacted sink.
